newsitem.title: INDIA: No turnaround seen in India cement market - official.
newsitem.headline: No turnaround seen in India cement market - official.

text.p: India's depressed cement market is unlikely to show any quick turnaround, a top official of the country's largest cement firm said.
"The current situation in the marketplace is not cheerful," S. Ganguly, executive vice chairman of Associated Cement Companies Ltd (ACC) told reporters on Wednesday night.
"Prices today are lower than what it was a year ago."
Ganguly said ACC has put on hold a new four-million-tonne a year cement project in southern Karnataka state until the market conditions improved.
"We are not pressing the button yet, though we are in state of readiness," he said. "We don't wish to commit large sums in an unfavourable market."
The project is estimated to cost 5.5 billion rupees.
ACC will be investing 3.0 billion rupees in 1997/98 on technology upgradation and expansion at its other plants.
He said he expects ACC's sales to grow to 11 million tonnes in the year to March 31, 1998 from 10 million tonnes, but price realisations were unpredictable.
ACC's net profit for 1996/97 (April-March) plunged to 769.2 million rupees from 2.27 billion in the year before because of stiff increases in input costs and poor market conditions.

The directors recommended a dividend of 30 rupees per share of 10 rupees face value, payable on higher capital after a three-for-five bonus share issue. It had paid a dividend of 70 rupees for 1995/96.
